headlines.article_text: Critical web security flaws spark global alarm: Google, OpenAI, Amazon Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Two critical vulnerabilities, collectively known as “PHP2Shell,” could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers. Governments worldwide have issued urgent security warnings, while Google, OpenAI and other tech companies have worked to identify vulnerabilities and protect affected systems. Amazon detected attempts to exploit the flaws before their public disclosure, but said it remains unclear how attackers obtained information about them. 21 October 2026, Baden-Württemberg, Stuttgart: When visiting the website of the Baden-Württemberg Ministry of the Interior, a warning message appears in the browser indicating a potential security issue. A serious security vulnerability is threatening websites worldwide; blogs, online stores, and news portals could become targets for attackers. The PHP vulnerability allows attackers to take over entire servers. Photo: Bernd Weißbrod/dpa (Photo by Bernd Weißbrod/picture alliance via Getty Images) Picture Alliance | Picture Alliance | Getty Images The tech world is racing to implement fixes after the discovery of critical security vulnerabilities in software used to power much of the internet. The software, known as PHP, is an open-source programming language widely used to power websites and web applications. The discovery of the flaws prompted urgent warnings from governments worldwide, while tech giants including Google, OpenAI and Amazon have been involved in efforts to uncover the vulnerabilities, detect potential attacks and protect affected systems. The two vulnerabilities, collectively known as "PHP2Shell," could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers, potentially exposing sensitive data, according to cybersecurity researchers. While not every website using PHP is necessarily vulnerable, the software's widespread use has raised concerns about the potential scale of attacks. The U.S. National Security Agency on Wednesday urged organizations using PHP to prepare security updates addressing the vulnerabilities, warning that the flaws could provide attackers with direct access to server file systems and databases. The agency recommended taking affected systems offline until the vulnerabilities are fully addressed if immediate updates are not possible. The Federal Bureau of Investigation also warned that malicious actors could exploit the vulnerabilities to execute code remotely, putting sensitive data and networks at risk. Cybersecurity authorities in Singapore , the United Kingdom , Australia , Canada and the European Union have issued similar alerts, underscoring concerns about the potential impact on businesses, government agencies and other organizations that rely on PHP-based systems. Amazon said its threat intelligence team had detected attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were publicly disclosed, using its MadPot threat detection system, which monitors suspicious activity across internet-facing infrastructure. It said the findings suggest malicious actors were already attempting to exploit the vulnerabilities. However, Amazon said it remains unclear how the attackers obtained information about the flaws ahead of their disclosure. Meanwhile, Google and OpenAI highlighted the growing role of artificial intelligence in identifying and addressing cybersecurity threats. Google said its cybersecurity unit Wiz used AI models to help find and investigate the vulnerabilities, while its Gemini AI contributed to efforts to assess the flaws, test potential attacks and verify security patches. OpenAI said researchers working with its AI models had also helped uncover critical vulnerabilities in PHP. The company said it had spent the past two months leading a coalition of software maintainers, cybersecurity researchers and security providers to coordinate fixes and prepare protective measures ahead of public disclosure. The ChatGPT maker described the flaws as among the most significant security issues in recent memory, highlighting both the potential of advanced AI systems to identify vulnerabilities in widely used software and the risk that similar capabilities could be exploited by cybercriminals. Cloudflare, which provides cybersecurity and website infrastructure services, said it had deployed protections against the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities through its web application firewall. The company said its measures were designed to help block malicious requests targeting affected systems, providing an additional layer of defense as organizations work to install software updates. The PHP development team has released security fixes, with authorities urging website operators to identify affected versions and apply the updates as quickly as possible. The episode underscores how vulnerabilities in widely used software can pose risks across industries and borders, even as AI increasingly plays a role in helping security researchers uncover and address those weaknesses. The stock rose about 2.5% in extended trading. Earnings per share : $3.83 Revenue : $64.60 billion vs $63.37 billion It's not clear if earnings were comparable to the $5.75 per share expected by analysts. Revenue jumped 26% from a year ago. "We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model," said CEO Mark Zuckerberg in the earnings release. For the fourth quarter, Meta said it expects revenue of between $73 billion and $76 billion, or $74.5 billion at the middle of the range. Analysts expected $73.73 billion, according to LSEG. The initial success of the Muse AI personal assistant tool that debuted in September helped Meta end September with its best month on Wall Street since 2022. Meta isn't the first to create a digital assistant that can organize people's email and scan the web for headphone deals, but the company's empire, which includes Facebook and Instagram, has helped introduce AI agents to the masses. At the same time, Meta and its AI chief Alexandr Wang have continued rolling out new foundation models and related updates at a speedy clip, including Muse Wonder , which was released last Monday. headlines.summary: Tesla reported better-than-expected third-quarter results.
headlines.article_text: Tesla (TSLA) Q3 2026 earnings report Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tesla reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Automotive revenue fell 3% from a year earlier. Tesla shares are down 14% this year, underperforming the rest of megacap tech. In this article TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 0:48 00:48 Tesla beats on Q3 revenue and earnings expectations Closing Bell: Overtime Tesla reported better-than-expected third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday, even as automotive revenue dropped. The stock slid more than 3% in extended trading. Here's how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 48 cents adjusted vs. 43 cents estimated Revenue: $28.05 billion vs. $27.9 billion estimated Tesla's earnings report lands a day after CEO Elon Musk told investors on SpaceX's quarterly call that it would be a "good idea" for his two companies to merge, and said the boards at both have formed special committees to discuss a possible tie-up. "I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield," Musk said on the call, responding to a question about a potential merger. Musk addressed the matter in his opening comments on the Tesla call, but didn't provide any additional information. "I think I said everything that should be said yesterday," he said. Tesla's revenue was down slightly flat from a year earlier, when the company generated sales of $28.24 billion, according to the earnings deck. In Tesla's core automotive business, revenue declined 3% from a year earlier to $20.56 billion in the quarter. Energy revenue fell 16% to $2.88 billion. Balancing out the declines were gains in Tesla's services and other revenue. Sales there climbed 33% from a year ago to $4.61 billion. Tesla blamed its lackluster automotive revenue and profits on lower average sales prices for its cars during the quarter, and trouble securing battery supplies to make enough vehicles to fulfill a backlog of orders. Net income attributable to common share holders plummeted 29% to $787 million, or 22 cents a share, from $1.11 billion, or 32 cents a share, a year earlier, Tesla said. The drop in profitability reflects a surge in spending on Optimus humanoid robots and other artificial intelligence initiatives. Capital expenditures more than doubled from a year earlier to $3.73 billion. Free cash flow plunged by 62% year over year to $1.53 billion, after Tesla turned free cash flow negative in the second quarter. A Tesla Bot, also known as Optimus, is displayed beside Tesla logos at a promotional exhibition in a shopping mall on September 18, 2026, in Hong Kong, China. Cheng Xin | Getty Images Tesla said uptake of its FSD (Supervised), a partially automated driving system the company sells for $99 per month in the U.S., grew by 20 percentage points from the second quarter. Active FSD subscriptions increased 67% from a year earlier to 1.74 million. "We believe that FSD is driving demand in markets where it is available, and we continue to work with regulators to get it approved in other markets," the company said in its investor deck. Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's vice president of Autopilot, said on the earnings call that the company plans to give some customer cars access to its forthcoming FSD (Unsupervised) systems around the second quarter of next year. Tesla is testing its Cybercab, a bronze two-seater designed for use as a robotaxi, but it's not yet sold to individuals. Musk said on the call that "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and transport-as-a-service." The company plans to bring Cybercab to cities beyond Austin, Texas, this year, Taneja said, paying attention to operating costs like maintenance, charging and cleaning. Musk said the company's driverless Robotaxi fleet will start to contribute to the company's financials in 2027. That fleet now includes 362 Model Y Robotaxi, and 449 Cybercab vehicles authorized for driverless operations in Texas, according to the state's Department of Motor Vehicles, "It's not like going to move the needle this quarter," Musk said, "I think it starts to become noticeable in Q2 and then probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year." Barring regulatory intervention and protectionism, Musk predicted that Tesla "will end up doing a majority of all passenger miles on Earth in any country where it is allowed to operate freely." Tesla said its auto sales in Canada, Japan, Taiwan and Australia hit new records during the quarter. However, the company has gotten meager growth out of its core market of late as Chinese EV makers such as BYD and Xiaomi gained popularity in Asia and Europe with affordable and innovative EVs. Tesla was also hit last year by the end of a federal EV tax credit. Earlier this month, Tesla reported vehicle deliveries for the third quarter of 486,532, about 2% below the year-ago number. Deliveries are the closest approximation of sales reported by Tesla but are not precisely defined in its shareholder communications. One of Tesla's big investments is in a semiconductor factory that it's building with SpaceX and Intel in Grimes County, Texas. That partnership with SpaceX along with other areas of overlap, including work on Tesla's recently announced Roadster refresh, fueled intensifying speculation that Musk's companies were on the verge of combining in what would be a historic transaction. On Optimus, Musk said Tesla is "making good progress" on the AI systems that control the robots in development. He said there's "still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks." Musk said he expects current issues around electromechanical design, reliability, usage duration, and AI to be "solved around the end of next year." headlines.title: CoreWeave’s market confidence erodes as bond yields spike and stock sinks
headlines.summary: CoreWeave shares are down 29% in October, and the spreads in its credit default swaps are widening.
headlines.article_text: CoreWeave’s market confidence erodes as bond yields spike, stock sinks Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave's stock is down 29% this month, and the spreads in its credit default swaps are widening. The company's elevated bond yield is prompting investors to question what additional financing options are available. "Sentiment is decidedly negative," Andrew Keches, credit analyst at Barclays, wrote in a note to clients this week, referring to AI bonds. In this article CRWV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator appears after the company's initial public offering at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York on March 28, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images CoreWeave is facing a crisis of confidence on Wall Street that's playing out in real time among equity and bond investors. With interest rates spiking and AI build-out concerns mounting, debt-heavy neoclouds like CoreWeave are being viewed by many market participants as the most vulnerable trade in the artificial intelligence space. "Sentiment is decidedly negative," Andrew Keches, a credit analyst at Barclays, wrote in a note to clients on Tuesday, referring broadly to corporate debt in tech. Keches highlighted the "speed at which AI vibes are shifting on a day-to-day basis." CoreWeave, which went public in March of last year and reached a peak market cap of about $90 billion three months later, is now valued at roughly $34 billion, with its stock down 29% this month. Its unsecured debt, meanwhile, is sporting a yield of about 15%. CoreWeave's stock move this month The spread on CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, is up 164% in the past year and 30% in October. It last stood at nearly 1,067 basis points, or 10.67%. CoreWeave declined to comment. The story is playing out across the neocloud sector. Shares of Nebius are down 27% this month, while IREN's stock is down 32%. In Australia, shares of data center operator NextDC plunged 40% on Wednesday after the company slashed its annual earnings forecast. Earlier this month, Australian data center company Firmus scrapped its planned initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions. U.K. neocloud Nscale is now under the microscope as investors wait to see whether the Nvidia-backed company will go through with its IPO. The company filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange last month. A representative from Nscale declined to comment. On hold until midterms CoreWeave is the biggest of the pack, and is intimately tied to the U.S. AI market. Nvidia is its top institutional investor, with a stake of about 9%, according to FactSet. And more than two-thirds of CoreWeave's revenue last year came from Microsoft . That's put a spotlight on CoreWeave's financials and its ability to remain viable. The company has about $20.7 billion in debt coming due through 2030 and another $14.9 billion thereafter, with the prospects of higher interest rates on future financing. Sources on credit desks told CNBC that the high-yield debt market is effectively on hold until after the midterm elections in two weeks given ongoing concerns about the political pushback that data centers are facing. One source, who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter, said fixed income investors "want permitting and regulatory requirements to be substantially resolved" before they commit financing. "Given recent turbulence, pausing makes sense," Seth Meyer, global head of client portfolio management at Janus Henderson, said in an interview. watch now VIDEO 2:39 02:39 CoreWeave falls amid AI debt fears Power Lunch CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator, who co-founded the company in 2017 initially as a crypto-mining venture, sent a memo to employees on Thursday, which CNBC obtained, to try and tamp down concern. Intrator stressed that the company maintains a range of funding options. "Our financing model combines infrastructure-backed borrowing, corporate debt, equity, and customer prepayments," Intrator wrote. He added that the company has "additional flexibility to raise equity over time as market conditions and our capital needs warrant." CoreWeave had $5.5 billion of cash and equivalents at the end of the second quarter. The company is expected to report third-quarter results next month. Analysts expect negative free cash flow in the period to swell to $10.1 billion, the highest since the company started reporting quarterly financials, according to FactSet. One issue being debated heading into the report is how much more capital CoreWeave needs to raise. Rob Oliver, a software analyst at Baird, is estimating roughly $30 billion in 2027. "Earnings may address financing measures to shore up confidence," Oliver said in an interview. "But they wouldn't need that capital until the first quarter." Another question is whether Nvidia will step in if necessary? Nvidia, which supplies the graphics processing units that CoreWeave rents out, invested $2 billion in January for a 10% stake. The purchase price was $87.20 a share. The stock is now trading at $61.82 even after jumping 6% the day of the announcement. While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said last week that CoreWeave doesn't need a backstop, some investors say the chip giant's further participation may be necessary if credit conditions continue to worsen. Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Analysts at Goldman Sachs , JPMorgan Chase and Barclays have put out bullish notes on the company this week, highlighting the company's GPU-backed loans and its solid list of investment-grade customers like Microsoft and Meta . Goldman analysts emphasized the company's strength in the market relative to many of its neocloud competitors. "Not all neoclouds are created equal," they wrote, in upgrading their rating to buy from hold. "CoreWeave is likely in the top quartile of neoclouds, if not the top decile, when measured on performance and ability to execute." — CNBC's Michelle Fox and Jordan Novet contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: META, TSLA, LRCX, IBM Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading. Tesla — Elon Musk's auto manufacturer shed earlier gains and last traded down 2%. Tesla posted beats on the top and bottom lines in the third quarter . The company earned 48 cents per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $28.05 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for 43 cents a share and $27.88 billion. International Business Machines — Shares wiped their earlier gains and slipped 2%. The company reported adjusted earnings of $2.95 per share for the third quarter, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's expectations for $2.86 per share. Revenue also beat estimates, and IBM now expects free cash flow for full-year 2026 to increase by more than $1 billion over the year prior. Rollins — The pest control company saw shares fall more than 7% after third-quarter results missed the Street's estimates. Rollins earned 33 cents a share on $1.09 billion in revenue, while the FactSet consensus sought 34 cents a share and $1.11 billion. Meta Platforms — The social media giant gained 3% in extended trading after revenue came in ahead of analysts' estimates. Third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion topped the LSEG consensus call for $63.37 billion. The midpoint of its fourth-quarter sales guidance was also above the Street's estimates. CSX — The railway company gained 4% after third-quarter earnings beat expectations. CSX earned 57 cents per share on revenue of $4.02 billion, while analysts surveyed by LSEG called for 53 cents a share and $3.96 billion. Revenue per unit increased 7% in the period, compared to the StreetAccount consensus expectation for 5.9% growth. Las Vegas Sands – Shares of the resort company fell 2% after the company posted disappointing third-quarter results. Las Vegas Sands posted adjusted earnings of 54 cents per share on revenue of $3.22 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting 69 cents in earnings per share and $3.35 billion in revenue. Lam Research — The semiconductor manufacturing equipment company dropped more than 5%. Lam sees second-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.33 per share, plus or minus 15 cents, on revenue of $8.60 billion, plus or minus $400 million. That compares to analysts' expectation for $2.31 per share and revenue of $8.53 billion. SAP SE — Shares of the software company advanced 4% after earnings and revenue surpassed analysts' estimates in the third quarter. QuantumScape – Shares of the company behind lithium-metal battery tech surged more than 9%. QuantumScape announced plans for a 100 megawatt-hour solid-state battery production line for artificial intelligence data centers. Molina Healthcare – The managed healthcare services provider dipped 4%. While third-quarter results beat expectations, premium revenue guidance for the full year is unchanged at roughly $42 billion. The company's guidance metrics across all segments are also reaffirmed. Molina president and CEO Joseph Zubretsky said, "With the apparent plateauing of medical cost trend, which remains at elevated levels, and the strength of recent rate updates for 2027, we believe we are likely observing the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins." CNBC's Davis Giangiulio, Sean Conlon, Sarah Min and Paulina Likos contributed reporting.
